title: Java Lambda
learningObjectives: Explain lambda expressions as concise functional implementations.
Use inferred parameter types and expression bodies.
Use lambdas with collection operations and sorting.
Recognize effectively final variables captured by lambdas.

understand.concept: A lambda expression is a concise way to provide an implementation of a functional interface, which has one abstract method. A lambda can have parameters, an arrow and a body. Java can infer parameter types from the target functional interface. Lambdas are commonly used with Runnable, Comparator and collection operations. Local variables captured from an enclosing scope must be final or effectively final.
understand.whyItMatters: This topic equips Java learners to write robust programs using java lambda in real applications.
understand.analogy: Think of each language feature as a clearly labelled tool: choose it for the specific problem it is designed to solve.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace the Java language and library contracts; compile and test the actual behaviour.

explain.narrative: A lambda such as (a, b) -> a + b can implement a functional interface with a matching method signature. A single expression can omit braces and return; a block body uses braces and explicit return when needed. Use standard functional interfaces from java.util.function where appropriate. Lambdas improve readability when the operation is short and the target type is clear; avoid overly complex nested expressions.

examples.title: Runnable lambda
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Runnable task = () -> System.out.println("Running"); task.run(); } }
examples.explanation: The lambda implements Runnable's single abstract run method.

examples.title: Use a parameter
examples.code:
import java.util.function.Consumer;
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Consumer<String> greet = name -> System.out.println("Hi " + name); greet.accept("Asha"); } }
examples.explanation: Consumer accepts one value and returns no result.

examples.title: Return a value
examples.code:
import java.util.function.Function;
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Function<Integer, Integer> square = n -> n * n; System.out.println(square.apply(6)); } }
examples.explanation: Function maps an input value to a result.

examples.title: Sort with a lambda
examples.code:
import java.util.ArrayList;
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { ArrayList<Integer> nums = new ArrayList<>(); nums.add(9); nums.add(2); nums.add(5); nums.sort((a, b) -> Integer.compare(a, b)); System.out.println(nums); } }
examples.explanation: The lambda supplies the Comparator comparison rule.

examples.title: Use a predicate
examples.code:
import java.util.function.Predicate;
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Predicate<String> longWord = word -> word.length() > 4; System.out.println(longWord.test("collections")); System.out.println(longWord.test("Java")); } }
examples.explanation: Predicate evaluates a condition and returns a boolean.

practise.guidedTask: Build a small Java program that demonstrates java lambda. Predict the output before compiling with JDK 21.
practise.independentTask: Create a practical application using java lambda. Include at least two test cases, expected output, and an explanation of one important edge case.
hints: A lambda expression supplies an implementation for a functional interface with one abstract method.
Use a method reference when it expresses the same operation more clearly than a lambda body.
Check captured local variables: they must be final or effectively final, and keep side effects understandable.
practise.challenge: Extend one example into a small reusable component and document its error handling, ordering or concurrency guarantees as relevant.

questions.explanation: A lambda provides the implementation of a functional interface's single abstract method.

questions.prompt: Which symbol separates lambda parameters from its body?
questions.explanation: The arrow token introduces the lambda body.

questions.prompt: Which standard interface accepts one input and returns a boolean?
Which interface is suitable for an operation that consumes a value and returns no result?
questions.explanation: Consumer<T> defines accept(T) with no return value.

questions.prompt: What must a captured local variable be?
questions.explanation: A lambda can capture local variables only when they are final or effectively final.
